prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you put ketchup on a hot dog in the city of Chicago. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, members of the Committee, I appreciate the opportunity to clear my name of these grave and frankly baseless accusations. 

Let me state for the record, clearly and unequivocally: I am not now, nor have I ever been, a consumer of ketchup on a Chicago-style hot dog. 

The allegations brought forth by this committee are a witch hunt, cooked up by sympathizers of the Red Menace—and by "Red," of course, I mean Heinz. The cowardly witnesses who testified against me claim they saw me squeeze that sugary, abhorrent tomato paste onto a pure Vienna Beef frankfurter within city limits. This is a fabrication of the highest order! 

If you look at Exhibit A, my receipts from Portillo’s spanning the last decade, you will see a patriot’s record. You will see mustard. You will see neon green sweet relish, chopped white onions, fresh tomato slices, a kosher dill pickle spear, two sport peppers, and a dash of celery salt, all nestled in a poppy seed bun. The Magnificent Seven, Mr. Chairman! I "dragged it through the garden" exactly as our forefathers intended! 

Does a man who respects the sanctity of celery salt sound like a subversive to you?

I will admit, I was at the cookout in question. I will even admit that there was a bottle of ketchup in my immediate vicinity. But I swear to you, under penalty of perjury, *it was for the french fries*. I was merely passing the bottle to my nephew, who knows no better because he is from Ohio. I am trying to educate him, Mr. Chairman, not join him in his condiment treason.

I refuse to name names, but I know there are people in this very room who have secretly requested ketchup at Wrigley Field. You cannot break my spirit, and you will not tarnish my palate. I stand by the mustard, and I yield the balance of my time.
